battle.name: 米底亞-呂底亞戰爭
battle.theater: 安納托利亞東部哈爾斯河中游
battle.brief: 公元前590年，米底王基阿克薩瑞斯要求呂底亞王阿呂阿特斯交出流亡者，遭拒後開戰，五年互有勝負。第六年兩軍在哈爾斯河中游交鋒，正酣時白晝驟暗，日蝕使雙方停手議和。米底靠仿亞述的複合弓射手群與呂底亞的富庶重騎相抗，最後仍由波斯介入收場。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前六世紀末米底與呂底亞之間的一場總體戰，交戰地帶在安納托利亞高原東側，以哈爾斯河為天然分界線。米底一方是西亞大平原上的伊蘭語族國家：基阿克薩瑞斯於前625年推翻套在米底頭上的西徐亞人羈縻，隨後以波斯與巴比倫的同盟打垮新亞述帝國（前612年巴比倫陷亞述），把居美西斯、烏拉爾圖、伊朗高原諸部與札格羅斯山脈的部落整合成一個以哈爾斯河上游為核心的軍政體系。其軍隊在基阿克薩瑞斯手上被重整，不再是按氏族拼湊的民兵，而是仿亞述與烏拉爾圖的制度：國家配裝、分為戰略與戰術單位，軍官有固定的率領範圍，騎兵與射手另立建制，營帳與糧秣由專人管轄。呂底亞一方是安納托利亞西部的王國：首都薩迪斯在赫爾莫斯河谷，國王阿呂阿特斯與其子克羅伊索斯掌控王室的貴金屬礦脈與愛奧尼亞商路，家底遠勝米底。呂底亞的常備軍以重裝騎兵與鎧甲步兵為骨幹，弓手與投石手多為受雇的外來人，另有一支薩迪斯城防民兵。米底境內尚殘留新亞述的兵制與工匠，烏拉爾圖與西徐亞、辛梅里安系的弓手傳統也仍在；因此這場仗裡的兵器體系，幾乎就是亞述軍事的餘脈與其北方模仿者之間的碰撞，而亞述人自稱承自阿卡德人的弓法傳承，經過烏拉爾圖與新亞述的鍛鐵改裝後，正好被米底繼承。
countriesEn: This war was a general conflict between Media and Lydia in the late sixth century BC, fought in the eastern part of the Anatolian plateau with the Halys river as the natural dividing line. On the Median side stood an Iranian-speaking state of the great western Iranian plain: Cyaxares overthrew the Scythian yoke over the Medes in 625 BC, then, in alliance with Persia and Babylon, broke the Neo-Assyrian Empire (Babylon fell on Nineveh in 612 BC), and fused the peoples of Ecbatana, Urartu, the Iranian plateau and the Zagros ranges into a single military-political structure centred on the upper Halys. His army was reorganised: no longer a militia patched together from kinship groups, it followed the Assyrian and Urartian model, with the state outfitting the troops, the force divided into strategic and tactical units, each officer holding a fixed command area, cavalry and archers formed as separate establishments, and the camp and its supplies placed under dedicated managers. On the Lydian side stood a kingdom of western Anatolia: the capital Sardis lay in the valley of the Hermus, and King Alyattes and his son Croesus controlled the royal metal veins and the Aegean trade, and their resources far exceeded the Medes'. The Lydian standing army had heavy cavalry and armoured infantry as its backbone, with archers and slingers largely hired from outside, plus a garrison militia for Sardis itself. The institutions of the Neo-Assyrian army and its craftsmen still survived inside Media, and the bow traditions of Urartu and of the Scythian and Cimmerian peoples were still alive; the weapon system in this war was therefore very nearly a collision between the aftermath of Assyrian warfare and its northern imitators, while the Assyrians themselves traced their bow practice back to the Akkadians, and it was that inheritance, reforged in Urartian and Neo-Assyrian iron, which the Medes took over.
people: 主導這場戰爭的是兩位國王與一位王子。米底王基阿克薩瑞斯（希臘文 Kuaxarēs，楔形文字名 ᴴuvaxšaθra，意為「良善的統治者」）是米底最重要的軍事改革者：他在推翻西徐亞人羈縻之後，把氏族民兵改編成由國家供裝的常備軍，並仿亞述與烏拉爾圖的編制劃分戰略與戰術單位；第狄奧多魯斯另稱他為 Astibaras，釋作「持矛者」。其子阿斯提亞格斯（Median Rštivaigah，「擲矛者」）在戰爭的第六年以米底王子身分迎娶呂底亞王阿呂阿特斯之女阿麗妮絲，兩家的姻親關係正是在日蝕停戰的同時訂下的；日後他成為米底國王，卻在國內被米底貴族架空，最終在前550年引波斯王居魯士入主，自身被取代。呂底亞王阿呂阿特斯是米雅德王朝的開創者居吉斯之子，他早年擊退西徐亞與辛梅里安人的侵擾，把呂底亞的勢力推到赫爾莫斯河以外的安納托利亞；他的子克羅伊索斯是呂底亞最後的國王（前585至前546年在位），以巨富聞名，其在德爾斐的奉獻與那根立在神廟前的金柱成為希臘世界的名勝。戰局最著名的技術性人物是米利都的泰利斯：希羅多德說他預言了那一場日蝕並以此中斷戰鬥，這段記載使日蝕預測在希臘思想史中成為標誌。最後是那些沒有留下名字的人：呂底亞雇來的伊奧尼亞弓手與重裝步兵雇傭兵團、米底的射手隊軍官與營務工匠，以及在前539年之後被波斯收編的各部落首領；他們的裝備與膽量，往往比國王的決策更快決定一場會戰的走向。
peopleEn: Two kings and a prince drove this war. Cyaxares, king of the Medes (Greek Kuaxarēs; in cuneiform ᴴuvaxšaθra, meaning good ruler) was the great military reformer of Media: after throwing off the Scythian yoke he converted the kinship militias into a standing army equipped by the state and divided the force into strategic and tactical units on the Assyrian and Urartian model; Diodorus Siculus also names him Astibaras, which he renders as spear-bearer. His son Astyages (Median Rštivaigah, spear-thrower) married Aryenis, the daughter of the Lydian king Alyattes, in the sixth year of the war, in the very same settlement that halted the fighting at the eclipse; he later became king of the Medes, was hollowed out by the Median nobility at home, and in 550 BC called in the Persian king Cyrus, being set aside himself. Alyattes, king of Lydia, was the son of Gyges, the founder of the Mermnad line; he had earlier thrown back the Scythian and Cimmerian incursions and carried Lydian power beyond the Hermus into Anatolia. His son Croesus was the last king of Lydia (585 to 546 BC), famous for his enormous wealth, and his dedications at Delphi and the golden column he set up before the temple became a landmark of the Greek world. The best known technical figure of the engagement is Thales of Miletus: Herodotus has him predict the eclipse and thus break off the fighting, and the story made eclipse prediction a landmark of Greek thought. Last come the people who left no names: the Ionian archers and mercenary companies of heavy infantry hired by Lydia, the officers of the Median arrow units and their camp craftsmen, and the chiefs of the tribes absorbed by Persia after 539 BC. Their equipment and their nerve often decided the course of a battle faster than the decisions of kings.
kits: 卡面上這件亞述長弓，是新亞述時期北方陸軍的標準射手兵器：木製弓臂，內貼角、外纏筋腱，張力時形成明顯的反曲，箭鏃用鐵，箭杆短而直，攜帶與上弦都適合騎在馬上或在車上作戰。亞述人靠弓與鐵的組合征服兩河流域，靠的就是弓兵在車上射、車兵靠弓兵開路這套配合；弓手的射速與射程使他們能在車陣尚未接敵時先削弱對方，車隊與騎兵才得以貼上。放到這場戰爭的體系裡看，這件弓的位置極為清楚：基阿克薩瑞斯重整米底軍隊時所仿的正是亞述與烏拉爾圖的樣子，而亞述王國在前612年崩解之後，亞述的兵器工匠、弓手傳統與大量鐵器仍散落在米底、烏拉爾圖與辛梅里安人手中；米底所謂仿亞述並非空話，而是摸得到的武器制度。呂底亞一方則是另一套搭配：重裝騎兵居前，鎧甲步兵列於其後，弓手與投石手在兩翼，鎧甲以青銅片與皮條綴合，頭盔常帶羽飾或獸形冠，長矛配短劍；弓手多為受雇的伊奧尼亞人與呂底亞本地射手，使用尺寸較小的複合弓，射速快而射程短，適合掩護車輪與正面。攻城方面，薩迪斯的城牆是石砌核心牆加土坯外牆，敵軍靠填土斜坡、掘地道與移動木塔逼近；薩迪斯的金銀精煉廠同時供應造幣所需的金與銀，王室的車比克是首見的雙金屬貨幣。運輸與補給靠騾、驢、牛車與人力，赫爾莫斯河谷的穀物與帕克托羅斯河的砂金是呂底亞軍力的物質底座。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card is the standard archery weapon of the Neo-Assyrian northern army: a wooden bow stave faced with horn on the inside and wrapped with sinew on the outside, taking a marked recurve under tension, with iron arrowheads and short straight shafts, easy to carry and to string on horseback or from a chariot. The Assyrians conquered the river valleys of Mesopotamia with the combination of the bow and iron, and the combination that did it was precisely bowmen shooting from chariots while the chariot crews rode behind the archers; the rate of fire and the range of the bow let them weaken the enemy before their own line closed, and only then could the chariots and the cavalry make contact. Within the system of this particular war the position of that bow is perfectly clear: the model Cyaxares followed when he reorganised the Median army was the Assyrian and Urartian one, and after the Assyrian kingdom collapsed in 612 BC the craftsmen, the bow traditions and a large stock of iron remained scattered among the Medes, the Urartians and the Cimmerians. The Median claim to imitate Assyria was not an empty phrase but a weapon system that could be handled in the hand. The Lydian side ran on a different combination: heavy cavalry in front, armoured infantry behind, archers and slingers on the wings, armour assembled from bronze plates and leather thongs, helmets often carrying plumes or animal crests, long spears with short swords; the archers were mostly hired Ionian and native Lydian bowmen using smaller composite bows, fast in rate of fire but short in range, well suited to covering the wheels and the front. For siege work the walls of Sardis were a stone core faced with mud brick, and the enemy came on by earthen ramp, by mining under the walls and by moving wooden towers; the gold and silver refinery of Sardis at the same time supplied the metal for the royal coinage, the bimetallic croeseid being the first coin of its kind. Transport and supply rested on mules, donkeys, ox carts and human porters, and the grain of the Hermus valley together with the gold dust of the Pactolus formed the material base of Lydian military power.
tactics: 交戰雙方的戰術都帶著安納托利亞高原與伊朗高原的特色。呂底亞的長處是騎兵：馬上射手與重裝騎兵並用，衝鋒前先以箭雨覆蓋敵陣，再以密集騎隊正面撞擊，這種打法需要寬闊的河谷與緩坡作騎兵戰場，哈爾斯河中游的沖積地正是這樣的地方。米底則靠步騎配合的縱深：步兵以長矛結陣，射手分列前鋒或兩翼，騎兵置於陣後與側翼待命，等敵騎衝陣後散開、露出缺口時再以矛陣與車隊反覆打擊。基阿克薩瑞斯所設的戰術單位與後來波斯軍的師團、大隊編制極為接近，便於分段投入。戰役過程本身留下了幾種典型交戰：頭五年裡有一場夜戰，雙方在黑暗中各自布陣而未能分出勝負；第六年的日蝕之戰，兩軍在哈爾斯河畔正面列陣，戰至白晝驟暗，士卒與統帥都停下來議和；再後來米底圍攻薩迪斯，呂底亞軍在夜裡出城反擊，攻破米底營壘，奪走大批器械與人馬，使米底一時無法再推進。補給是另一個關鍵：呂底亞遠征靠薩迪斯的穀物、車比克與沿海的商船，軍隊一旦離開赫爾莫斯河谷，就得沿路徵發；米底則靠埃克巴塔那與哈爾斯河上游的倉儲與路段供給，山路運力低，冬季不便長遠投射，所以雙方多半在春末至初秋交鋒，戰期拖長對缺糧的米底更為不利。
tacticsEn: The tactics of both sides carried the character of the Anatolian and the Iranian plateaus. The Lydian strength was cavalry: mounted archers and heavy horsemen were used together, the front being covered with a shower of arrows before a compact column of riders charged home, and such a style of fighting needed broad valley floors and gentle slopes to serve as a cavalry battlefield, which is exactly what the alluvial ground of the middle Halys provided. Media relied instead on depth of infantry and horse: spearmen closed into a phalanx, archers were posted at the front or on the wings, and the cavalry was held in reserve at the rear and on the flanks, waiting for the enemy horse to break up and open a gap before the spear wall and the chariots struck again and again. The tactical units Cyaxares created were very close to the divisions and brigades of the later Persian army, which made it possible to feed the fight in increments. The course of the war itself preserved several typical engagements: in the first five years there was a night battle in which the two sides deployed in the dark and could not separate the result; in the sixth year, the battle of the eclipse, the two armies drew up in line on the bank of the Halys and the fighting grew hot until day turned suddenly to night, and the soldiers and their commanders alike stopped and made terms; later still, when the Medes were besieging Sardis, the Lydian army sallied out by night, broke into the Median camp and took a great quantity of equipment and men, so that Media could not advance for a time. Supply was the second key. The Lydian expeditions drew on the grain, the croeseids and the coastal shipping of Sardis, and once an army left the Hermus valley it had to live off the country it marched through; Media drew on the storehouses and the road system of Ecbatana and the upper Halys, and mountain roads carry little, and the winter does not favour long projection of force, so the two sides usually fought from late spring into early autumn, and a drawn-out war told harder against Media for want of food.
data: 可核對的數字不多，但有幾個是硬的。第一是時間：希羅多德記此戰打了五年，第六年那一戰才遇上日蝕；配合公元前590年的起算，第六年正落在公元前585年，而唯一符合「交戰正酣、白晝驟暗、地點在安納托利亞」的日蝕，就是公元前585年5月28日的那一次。第二是前後局勢：戰前米底已擺脫西徐亞人的羈縻二十八年，亞述帝國則於公元前612年被巴比倫與米底聯軍攻滅；換言之這場仗開打時，亞述的軍制傳統已散佚近二十年。第三是距離與地理：薩迪斯在赫爾莫斯河谷，哈爾斯河自東向西橫切安納托利亞高原，兩地之間的道路約三百五十至四百公里；米底都城埃克巴塔那在哈爾斯河東南，距薩迪斯約七百公里，調度全靠陸路，沒有可通行的河道。第四是物質：呂底亞的雙金屬車比克是當時最精密的錢幣之一，約合七克黃金配六至七克白銀，其成色要求薩迪斯同時精煉金銀，這在當時是獨一無二的做法；薩迪斯金銀精煉廠的廢渣說明當時冶煉的規模可觀，而城內出土的大量來自希臘本土的陶器，又說明呂底亞的富裕是靠愛奧尼亞商路變現的。第五是兵員：雙方出動人數沒有任何可靠數字，希羅多德不記兵數，同時期的編年也沒有為這場仗留下人數；可以確定的只是呂底亞的騎兵是兩軍勝負的關鍵，而基阿克薩瑞斯的常備軍按戰略與戰術單位編組，若按同時期近東的經驗推算，野戰兵力在數萬量級，任何十萬大軍的說法都應打折扣。本目錄所填的月份是按前590年開春外交破裂、當年未能決戰而推的，並非文獻記載。
dataEn: There are not many numbers that can be checked, but a few are hard. The first is time: Herodotus says the war lasted five years and that the sixth year was the one in which the eclipse was encountered; combined with a starting date of 590 BC, the sixth year falls in 585 BC, and the only solar eclipse matching a battle in progress, a sudden loss of daylight and a location in Anatolia is the one of 28 May 585 BC. The second is the situation before and after: the Medes had been free of the Scythian yoke for twenty-eight years, and the Assyrian empire had been destroyed by the allied Babylonians and Medes in 612 BC; in other words, when this war opened, the Assyrian military tradition had been dispersed for nearly twenty years. The third is distance and geography: Sardis lay in the valley of the Hermus, the Halys cut the Anatolian plateau from east to west, and the road between the two ran roughly three hundred and fifty to four hundred kilometres; the Median capital Ecbatana lay southeast of the Halys at about seven hundred kilometres from Sardis, and everything had to move by road, as there was no navigable waterway. The fourth is material: the bimetallic croeseid was among the most refined coins of its age, roughly seven grams of gold against six or seven of silver, and that standard required Sardis to refine gold and silver at the same time, which was without parallel at the time; the slag heaps of the Sardis refinery show the scale of the workings, while the quantities of Greek pottery found in the city show how Lydian wealth was cashed in through the Aegean trade. The fifth is the numbers of men: no reliable figure for either army exists, Herodotus gives no numbers of troops, and no chronicle of the period records any for this war; what can be established is that Lydian cavalry was the deciding arm, and that Cyaxares's standing army was organised into strategic and tactical units, so that by the experience of the near east the field forces must have been in the tens of thousands, and every claim of a hundred thousand men should be heavily discounted. The month entered in this record is inferred from the collapse of the diplomacy in the spring of 590 BC and the absence of any decisive engagement that year; it is not stated by the sources.
cause: 直接導火線有明確記載：基阿克薩瑞斯派使者到呂底亞，要求阿呂阿特斯交出一批流亡者（希臘史家稱之為求庇者，其中多為在西徐亞人撤走後流落呂底亞的西徐亞與辛梅里安餘部），阿呂阿特斯拒絕，戰端因此開啟。深一層的原因是新亞述崩解後留下的權力真空：公元前612年巴比倫與米底聯軍攻滅亞述王國，亞述在安納托利亞東部的行省、鐵匠與軍制傳統一下子無人收拾，哈爾斯河兩側出現多個互相爭奪的小政權，米底要做的第一件事就是把這條河東岸的山地與河谷收進自己的軍政體系；呂底亞則要阻止米底把手伸到自己這邊。再深一層是貿易與資源：呂底亞靠薩迪斯的金銀礦與愛奧尼亞的商路維持富裕與兵源，米底則需要下游的穀物、錫與通往兩河的商道；兩家的邊界因此不是一條想像出來的線，而是哈爾斯河這條可通行的實體線。個人層面上，兩國君主都剛經歷過內部危機：米底王推翻西徐亞人統治不久，軍隊還是拼湊的氏族民兵，需要一場對外戰爭來建立王權的正當性；呂底亞王則剛把西徐亞與辛梅里安人趕出國土，軍隊經過實戰，也需要一個能證明國力的目標。這五年的互有勝負因此既是邊界摩擦，也是兩套新軍制的實戰考試。
causeEn: The immediate occasion is explicitly recorded: Cyaxares sent envoys to Lydia demanding that Alyattes hand over a body of refugees, whom the Greek historians call suppliants and who were largely Scythian and Cimmerian remnants who had taken refuge in Lydia after the Scythians withdrew; Alyattes refused, and the war began. A layer deeper is the power vacuum left by the collapse of the Neo-Assyrian empire. In 612 BC the allied armies of Babylon and Media destroyed the Assyrian kingdom, and the provinces, the smiths and the military institutions of Assyria in eastern Anatolia were suddenly left without anyone to collect them, so that a number of small states on both banks of the Halys began to compete with one another; the first task of Media was to draw the hills and valleys on the east bank of that river into its own military-political structure, while Lydia's task was to stop Media from reaching across to its side. A layer deeper still is trade and resources: Lydia maintained its wealth and its recruitment from the gold and silver veins of Sardis and from the Aegean trade routes, while Media needed the grain, the tin and the caravan roads of the lower river; the frontier between the two was therefore not an imaginary line but a real and passable one, the Halys. At the personal level, both monarchs had just come through an internal crisis. The Median king had thrown off the Scythians only shortly before, and his army was still a patched-together militia of kinship groups that needed a foreign war to establish the legitimacy of kingship; the Lydian king had just driven the Scythians and Cimmerians out of his country, his troops were already battle-hardened, and he too needed a target that would demonstrate the strength of the state. The five years of mixed success were therefore at once a friction of borders and a field examination of two newly built military systems.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接成果有限，長遠影響卻不小。第一，兩家的邊界從此固定在哈爾斯河一線：呂底亞沒有被米底吞掉，米底也沒有拿到安納托利亞西部的通路，兩國進入一種緊張但可控的共處，日蝕停戰與阿麗妮絲、阿斯提亞格斯的婚約成了這段共處的象徵與保險。第二，戰爭把米底的國家制度推到前台：基阿克薩瑞斯的常備軍與分區編制，是後來波斯王國的省制與軍區制的直接前身；波斯君主日後給阿斯提亞格斯與米底貴族留下的極高待遇，正可以回溯到米底在兩河世界本來就有的貴族傳統。第三，呂底亞的財富被捲入了西亞的新強權：阿斯提亞格斯在前550年召居魯士入主米底，呂底亞王克羅伊索斯隨即進攻波斯，於普特里亞與薩迪斯前線連敗，最終在公元前546年失去王國；呂底亞的雙金屬車比克與金銀精煉技術從此進入波斯國庫，薩迪斯也成為波斯的一個行省。西方世界記住的不是這場戰爭本身，而是它的主顧：日蝕被泰利斯預言而使戰鬥中止的故事，在希臘世界被寫成理性戰勝恐懼的範例，泰利斯因此名留史冊，呂底亞與米底的名字也隨之傳遍地中海。希臘詩人與哲學家從此把安納托利亞的中部高原當成文明的邊界；四百多年後，希臘聯軍渡海東來時，爭的仍是這條界線的不同段落，呂底亞的舊土就是其中最早被捲入的那一塊。
impactEn: The immediate results of the war were limited, but its long effects were not. First, the frontier between the two countries was fixed on the line of the Halys: Lydia was not swallowed by Media, and Media gained no passage into western Anatolia, so the two entered a tense but manageable coexistence, of which the halt at the eclipse and the marriage of Aryenis to Astyages became both the symbol and the insurance. Second, the war pushed the Median institutions of state into the open: the standing army and the division into districts organised by Cyaxares are the direct ancestor of the satrapies and the military districts of the later Persian kingdom, and the very generous treatment that the Persian kings afterwards accorded Astyages and the Median nobility can be traced back to an aristocratic tradition that Media had possessed in the world of the two rivers all along. Third, Lydian wealth was drawn into the new power of the west: in 550 BC Astyages called Cyrus in to take over Media, the Lydian king Croesus at once struck at Persia, was beaten in the fighting before Pteria and before Sardis, and in 546 BC lost his kingdom; the bimetallic croeseids and the gold and silver refining of Lydia passed into the Persian treasury, and Sardis became a province of Persia. What the western world remembered was not the war itself but its occasion: the story of the eclipse foretold by Thales, which stopped the battle, was written up in the Greek world as the type case of reason overcoming fear, Thales was made a name in history, and the names of Lydia and Media travelled with him round the Mediterranean. Greek poets and philosophers from then on treated the central highlands of Anatolia as a frontier of civilisation, and when the Greek coalition came across the sea more than four centuries later it was still fighting over different stretches of that frontier, of which the old land of Lydia was the first part to be drawn in.
result: 若只看米底與呂底亞之間，這場戰爭沒有勝負可言。頭五年雙方互有勝敗，第六年的哈爾斯河之戰在日蝕中停成和局；此後戰端再起，米底一度攻到薩迪斯城下，卻在夜戰中被呂底亞反攻，營壘被破，攻勢瓦解。最終決定呂底亞命運的不是米底，而是更西邊的波斯：米底王子阿斯提亞格斯在前550年被本國貴族架空，轉而引居魯士入主；居魯士平定米底後，克羅伊索斯仍不自量，於前547年聯絡安納托利亞諸邦進攻波斯，先在普特里亞失利，薩迪斯被圍後在公元前546年陷落，國王被帶到波斯，成為流傳至今的克羅伊索斯之富這則故事的主角。就軍史而言可以確定的有幾點：其一，戰爭證明新興的米底常備軍在野戰上不遜於以財富立國的呂底亞，兩家因此都沒有被對方消滅；其二，日蝕的出現被兩軍領袖當作足以中止戰爭的信號，說明這場仗仍舊在祭祀、占卜與天象的框架裡被理解；其三，呂底亞的滅亡不是米底一手造成，這一點在後來的記述裡常被混淆。戰爭的真正結果，是安納托利亞中部高原從兩個王國的邊界，變成一個新帝國的腹地。
resultEn: If one looks only at Media and Lydia, this war had no victor. In the first five years the two sides had their successes and their defeats, and the battle of the Halys in the sixth year was broken off into a truce by the eclipse; the war then flared up again, the Medes came as far as the walls of Sardis, and were there broken in a night action by a Lydian counter-stroke that destroyed their camp and dissolved the offensive. What finally settled the fate of Lydia was not Media but Persia, further east: Astyages was hollowed out by his own nobility in 550 BC and turned to Cyrus instead; after Cyrus had settled Media, Croesus, refusing to accept the fact, struck at Persia in 547 BC with the help of the Anatolian states, was beaten at Pteria, and after the siege Sardis fell in 546 BC, the king being carried off to Persia and becoming the hero of the story of the wealth of Croesus that has been handed down ever since. As military history, several things can be stated with confidence. First, the war showed that the new Median standing army was no inferior in the field to a Lydia made rich by its mines, so that neither country was destroyed by the other. Second, the appearance of the eclipse was treated by the commanders on both sides as a sign sufficient to stop the fighting, which shows that this war was still understood inside a framework of sacrifice, divination and the reading of the heavens. Third, the fall of Lydia was not the work of Media alone, a point that is often confused in later accounts. The real result of the war was that the central highlands of Anatolia passed from being the border of two kingdoms to being the interior of a new empire.
